# PEN-4518 — assert from inside the Job pod that the pre-push publish guard is reachable

Tracking: [PEN-4518](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-4518)

Recorded here rather than in `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md`: that file is frozen (BLO-34872) because concurrent appends to it conflict on GitHub's server-side merge and get ejected from the merge queue.

## What happened

On 2026-10-22 at 10:15:03Z, `de138f64b` (BLO-32734 phase 2b) reached production. It overlays an emptyDir on the PVC root for narrowed Job pods and re-exposes an allowlist of toolchain subpaths. `.local/share/paperclip-git-hooks` was not on that allowlist, so the PEN-3156 pre-push publish guard became invisible inside every agent Job pod, and **every agent in the fleet lost the ability to push for 2h17m**. #2928 added the entry; this change is the third Done-when bullet, the one that prevents a recurrence.

## Why no test caught it

The path is spelled by four independent consumers, and three test suites already covered it — all three were green throughout the outage. They had to be: **every individual string was correct.**

| consumer | spells the path in | covered by |
|---|---|---|
| the Helm seed that WRITES the hook | `statefulset.yaml` (`GIT_HOOKS_DIR`) | chart suite |
| the egress runtime that LOOKS for it | `github-git-egress-runtime.ts` (`DEFAULT_HOOKS_DIR`) | runtime suite |
| the Job manifest that MOUNTS it | `job-manifest.ts` (`ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS`) | manifest suite (added by #2928) |
| nothing asserted the composition | — | — |

What was wrong was not a string but the **mount topology underneath them**. No suite owns the join between "the seed wrote it" and "the Job can see it", and the two halves live in different repositories' test suites. The seed's own success log — `seed: installed the PEN-3156 pre-push publish guard hook in /paperclip/.local/share/paperclip-git-hooks` — was still true the entire time: it writes to the PVC, and the Job pod sees an overlay.

This is exactly the rule BLO-32734's own provenance entry wrote down and that the next change then broke:

> a path is not on the PVC because it is spelled `/paperclip/...`; it is on it when a derived writable mount covers it.

## 1. One home for the path

**Files:** `packages/adapter-utils/src/github-git-hooks-path.ts` (new), `github-git-egress-runtime.ts`, `job-manifest.ts`

`GIT_HOOKS_SUBPATH`, `DEFAULT_DATA_MOUNT_PATH`, `DEFAULT_HOOKS_DIR` and `hooksDirForDataMount()` now live in one side-effect-free module. The runtime re-exports `DEFAULT_HOOKS_DIR` from it (public API unchanged) and `ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS` derives its entry from `GIT_HOOKS_SUBPATH` instead of restating the literal — so the allowlist entry and the path the runtime consults can no longer disagree.

A new module rather than reusing `github-git-egress-runtime.ts`, which already exported the constant, because **that module is not safely importable**: it selects its hook leg on `process.argv[2] === "--pre-push-hook"` at import time with the entrypoint guard deliberately removed (the long comment there explains why removing it was correct). Importing it into the server's Job-manifest path to reach one string would pull that behaviour into the server process.

Helm renders shell and cannot import anything, so consumer 1 stays joined by the chart suite's regex — repointed at the new module, and the declarations kept to a plain `= "literal"` form it can read.

### The vendored adapters restate it, and a test holds the restatement down

The first revision of this change had both adapters `import ... from "@paperclipai/adapter-utils/github-git-hooks-path"`. That typechecked in the monorepo and **failed both `Vendored * adapter` lanes** at `f41d8c9` with `TS2307: Cannot find module`. The export map was not the problem. Those lanes run `npm ci` inside the vendor directory, which resolves `@paperclipai/adapter-utils` from the **npm registry** at the version that package's own lockfile pins — `2026.428.0`, whose tarball ships `dist/server-utils.*` and nothing named `github-git-hooks-path`. `server-utils` imports fine from the same `"./*"` export precisely because it has already been published; a subpath that exists only in the working tree cannot resolve in a package built standalone.

Keeping the import would have traded this ticket's drift class for a **publish-ordering** class: the adapters would not build until adapter-utils cut a release and these two lockfiles bumped, with that ordering invisible from either side. Worse for a guard, the same unresolvable specifier sits on the Job-manifest path at runtime.

So each adapter carries `src/server/github-git-hooks-path.ts` restating the declarations, with a sibling `github-git-hooks-path.test.ts` that strips comments from both files and asserts the remaining executable content is identical. That is the same trade `pod-log-redactor.test.ts` already makes against `command-redaction.ts`, for the same standalone-build reason, and it is what the chart consumer needs regardless.

**This is not a retreat from one source of truth.** PEN-4518 was not caused by a copy existing — three consumers spelled this path independently and all three suites were green. It was caused by a copy that nothing compared. The byte-comparison is mutation-checked below.

## 2. The per-Job preflight — the actual recurrence-preventer

**Files:** `runtime-pin.ts` and `job-manifest.ts`, both adapters

`buildPrePushHookPreflightShell({ dataMountPath })` emits exactly one verdict to stderr, spliced in beside the PEN-4446 wrapper preflight and ahead of `workspaceSetup` for the same reason — that stage runs `git` against origin, so a verdict after it would describe a pod that had already reached GitHub.

- `ok` — executable hook where the runtime will look.
- `MASKED` — nothing at either path. The PEN-4518 shape. Names `ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS` and `/proc/mounts`, deliberately **not** the seed log.
- `OFF-MOUNT` — on the data volume but not where the runtime looks. `persistence.mountPath` has diverged; the runtime resolves from a constant and cannot read chart values.
- `NOT-EXECUTABLE` — present without `+x`. git runs no hook and reports nothing, so this case is otherwise entirely silent.

This asks the deployed pod instead of comparing source strings, which is the only form that survives a change in any of the four spellings *or* in the mount topology under them.

**Advisory, not fatal, and the asymmetry is deliberate.** The push path already fails closed — that is how the outage was found — so this cannot be what makes the guard binding, and there is nothing to gain by also killing the Job. There is something to lose: a false positive here would take the whole fleet down at second zero, against a missed verdict costing one confusing push refusal. What it buys is **time-to-diagnosis**. The verdict arrived as a push refusal 90 minutes into one agent's run; the same fact emitted at startup by every pod is greppable across the fleet before any work is stranded.

It reports presence and executability, **not** that the file is the real scanner — the same limit `prePushHookPresent` documents, for the same reason: the seed runs as uid 1000 and cannot write a file the agent could not rewrite. Named for what it observes.

The verdict text carries no bare `git` token. That is not style: `job-manifest.test.ts` scans the whole container command for unclassified `git` in command position, and prose inside an `echo` is indistinguishable from a call to that scan. Backtick-quoting it the way the breadcrumbs do is unavailable here, since these strings sit inside a double-quoted `echo` where a backtick is command substitution. The first draft tripped that guard; the wording changed rather than the scanner, which is what bounds every real `git` call in the Job.

## 3. Two drift repairs found on the way

- **`github-git-egress-runtime.test.ts`** staged the runtime's module graph into a temp boot directory from a hardcoded list of three filenames. Adding a fourth module broke all three end-to-end assertions with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The list now walks the relative-import graph. The deployed hook was never at risk — it runs out of a whole-directory `tsc` dist and nothing stages it file by file — but an enumeration that has to agree with a graph is the same defect class as the ticket itself.
- **`vendor/paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s/vitest.config.ts`** gained the `@paperclipai/adapter-utils` alias its claude-k8s sibling already had. Without it `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` collected **0 tests** from that directory — verified at `origin/master`, so this predates and is independent of PEN-4518. 142 tests were not running.

## Verification

- `packages/adapter-utils`: 71 tests (8 new) — including that the runtime's `DEFAULT_HOOKS_DIR` is the shared one.
- `paperclip-adapter-claude-k8s`: 23 files / 1667 tests — `tsc --noEmit` clean — including the 10 preflight tests, which **execute** the generated snippet under `sh` against fixtures in each of the four states.
- `paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s`: 20 files / 711 tests — `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `deploy/helm/paperclip/tests/agent-egress-path.test.mjs`: 25/25.

Both vendor lanes were run the way CI runs them: `npm ci --include=dev` in the vendor directory, then `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit`, then `vitest run`. That is what surfaced the TS2307 above — a monorepo-only typecheck cannot see it.

Mutation-checked rather than assumed green: removing `GIT_HOOKS_SUBPATH` from the allowlist fails #2928's manifest test; moving `DEFAULT_DATA_MOUNT_PATH` fails the chart join; relaxing the preflight's `-x` to `-e` fails the `NOT-EXECUTABLE` case. The new byte-comparison was mutation-checked in all three drift shapes — changing the literal, un-exporting a declaration, and reimplementing `hooksDirForDataMount`'s body each fail it, and the restored file passes.

## 4. Correction to the `NOT-EXECUTABLE` verdict (review follow-up)

The first revision's `NOT-EXECUTABLE` text said *"no hook runs and nothing is reported; every push from this pod publishes unscanned"*, and its docstring called the case *"otherwise entirely silent"*. **Both were wrong.** `prePushHookPresent` tests the hook with `accessSync(..., constants.X_OK)`, so a present-but-non-executable hook fails that check and the runtime throws `refusing to publish — no executable pre-push hook at …`. The push is **refused**, exactly as in `MASKED`; nothing publishes unscanned.

The distinction worth keeping is the remedy, not the consequence: `MASKED` means the mount does not reach this pod, `NOT-EXECUTABLE` means the mount is fine and the file needs `+x`. An alert-keyed marker announcing an unscanned-publish breach that is not happening would route its reader to incident response instead of to `chmod +x` — in a change whose entire value is an accurate diagnosis. Both the echo and the docstring now state the refusal and name the `+x` remedy, and the shell test pins the corrected text (including a negative assertion on the old `publishes unscanned` wording).
